title: Streamline routing policy pipeline and fallback resolution
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Background: The current smart routing stack evaluates multiple policy checks (region, SLAs, capacity tier, model compatibility) inline in the request hot path and applies a series of ad-hoc fallback heuristics. Over time this has grown complex, hard to test, and contributes to tail latency and sporadic misroutings when capacity signals are noisy.

Objective: Refactor the routing policy pipeline to a streamlined, deterministic evaluation graph that: (1) separates policy evaluation from capacity-aware routing in the hot path, (2) consolidates fallback selection into a single decision module with well-defined priority tiers, (3) removes duplicated regional probe logic, and (4) upgrades a few low-level dependencies to avoid subtle protobuf/grpc regressions.

Scope (in-scope):
- Introduce a lightweight policy-evaluation pass that pre-computes stable route candidates and metadata before capacity selection.
- Implement a canonical fallback resolver that uses explicit priority buckets (primary, soft-fallback, cold-fallback) instead of chained ad-hoc handlers.
- Replace regional probe actors with a single regional-affinity table and cached health snapshot updated by background reconciler.
- Upgrade protobuf from 3.20.x -> 3.23.x and grpc-java from 1.43 -> 1.55 to pick up performance and compatibility fixes.
- Add unit + integration tests that exercise concurrent evaluation and fallback failover.

Out of scope: global routing policy redesign, UI/Console changes, Dedicated autoscaler tuning (except where it affects API contracts).

Success criteria:
- p99 end-to-end routing latency for cold requests reduced by >=10% in microbenchmarks; 5–8% reduction in production p99 within canary windows.
- Deterministic fallback selection: post-change incident rate of routing misfires reduced by 90% compared to the baseline from last 30 days.
- No customer-facing errors introduced during staged rollout (feature-flagged canary).

Risks and mitigations:
- Dependency upgrades might change wire behavior: pin versions and add compatibility tests between runtime and control-plane stubs.
- Rollout could trigger new edge cases with capacity signals: use 5% canary traffic for 24h with synthetic traffic that stresses capacity and region failover.
- Logic errors during conversion: keep old pipeline behind a switch and implement automatic rollback on error SLO violations.

Plan / tasks (high-level):
1) Spike and microbench (2d): implement prototype evaluation pass + canonical fallback resolver.
2) Library changes (3d): refactor internal routing interfaces, add region-affinity cache module.
3) Tests and compatibility (3d): unit, integration, and compatibility tests for protobuf/grpc changes.
4) Safety + observability (2d): add tracing hooks, fallback decision logging, and a temporary dashboard.
5) Canary rollout (3d): 5% -> 25% -> 100% staged rollout with automated rollback.

Notes on approach: The evaluation pass will expose a compact struct (RouteCandidates) describing route candidates plus metadata (compatibility, cost score, regionAffinityScore). The hot-path capacity-aware allocator will consume RouteCandidates and remain intentionally minimal. This keeps the latency-sensitive portion small and easier to reason about. The fallback resolver is pure and deterministic given the same RouteCandidates snapshot and will be covered by exhaustive unit tests.

Operational signals to monitor: routing.p99_latency_ms, routing.error_rate, routing.fallback_rate, routing.fallback_type_breakdown, infra.capacity_signal_variance, canary.rollback_triggered.

Open questions:
- Do we need to persist RouteCandidates in the control-plane for cross-request correlation? (Tentatively no; keep ephemeral).
- Exact priority weighting between regionAffinityScore and cost: propose configuration flag with safe default (regionAffinityWeight=1.0, costWeight=0.5) for initial rollout.

Deliverables: design doc link, PRs, canary dashboard, migration plan, test matrix.

2025-02-14 - Sofia Chen (review): Code structure looks good. Request more coverage around concurrent region-affinity cache updates. Please add tests simulating delayed health reconciler updates and ensure fallback determinism when health snapshot lags. Also request a short compatibility test matrix for protobuf/grpc versions.

2025-02-19 - Liam Patel: Addressed Sofia's feedback. Added concurrency tests (concurrency_test.go) and compatibility tests that exercise proto stubs. Updated PR with changes and invited Rahul for second review. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/routing/pull/3478

2025-02-25 - Rahul Desai (review): Found an edge case when capacity signals transiently flip between regions during allocation. Added guard to prefer same-region candidate if score delta < 0.05 to avoid flapping. Also asked to expose a fallback_decision.trace_id in logs for easier post-mortem. Implemented both in PR #3478.

2025-03-01 - Liam Patel: Canary ready. Feature flag gate created (flag: routing.refactor.v2). Plan: 5% traffic for 24h with synthetic pressure; if no regressions, increase to 25% for 48h, then 100%. Added Grafana panel: routing/refactor-canary and Alert if error_rate > 0.5% or p99 increases > 20% relative baseline.
